A definition-record kind on the record contract, following the goal and claim pattern, so it gets history, supersede, search, recall, RAG export and CLI/MCP from one declaration. A non-functional requirement is a quality attribute scenario with a mandatory response measure. Status lifecycle proposed-by-agent, proposed, approved, retired; approved needs a person.

D-product-docs: an agent may accept requirements of the low-risk classes named by the knob requirements.agent_accept_classes (default: documentation only); a person accepts all others.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds (kind, template, gate, lens, role, lint set, importer, pack, job) is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

NOTE 2026-10-23 (queue dedupe review, qa-dupes): this task and RQM-model define the SAME kind, ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml. D-requirements-model (operator 2026-10-21) fixed ONE kind 'requirement' with class product|constraint|standard|policy and strength must|should|may, and RQM-decide says 'P-product-docs adds EARS/baseline fields to the same descriptor'. So read this task as an EXTENSION of RQM-model: the 'kind (functional, nfr, constraint, vendor)' field above becomes 'class' plus an nfr flag, vendor items stay in PD-vendor-kind, and EARS text, mandatory source[], response measure, parents and baseline are fields added to the RQM-model descriptor. No second requirement kind. Ordering: RQM-model first (both edit requirement.toml).

data.body: Contradiction found by the queue dedupe review 2026-10-23. Evidence: D-review-rounds-4 (operator 2026-10-21: project [review].max_rounds = 4; 5 REJECTED; 'lets say 4 or 5'); shipped default in ddflow/config_sections/review.py is still 2 and its doc text says 'default 2'; RV-round-cap (open) says 'cap at a knob default 2' for delta rounds, a premise (round 3+ is 36.7% precise) that predates the 4; lead directions of 2026-10-22/23 authorise a 5th round via 'review --force --gate G --reason' under 'the operator's 4-5 range', and recent waivers say 'operator-directed waiver after five rounds'; DX-review-delta-superseded and DX-review-concurrent-runs still describe a 2-round budget. B-gate-econ-review-budget (done) already counts delta rounds in max_rounds, so RV-round-cap's delta cap is redundant. Question for the operator: (1) is the cap 4 with a recorded 5th, or 5? (2) what is the SHIPPED default for other projects (2 or 4)? (3) is RV-round-cap dropped? RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: keep shipped default 2 and this project's 4; a 5th round is allowed only as 'review --force --reason' (recorded, reported), never a config of 5; abandon RV-round-cap as done by B-gate-econ-review-budget; reword the two DX bodies. Record the answer as decision D-review-rounds-4-r2 (supersedes D-review-rounds-4).

data.body: Contradiction found by the queue dedupe review 2026-10-23. Several accepted records each claim a slice of the always-loaded context with different units and numbers: LS-charter (done): MCP instructions <=1.5K chars and SessionStart <=1K chars; D-requirements-injection: always-on charter one line per MUST capped at 500 tokens ([requirements].charter_tokens); D-rules-charter: keep the rules charter; GP-brief: one policy charter plus a brief line; RA-brief: pending-approvals line 'within the lean charter'; B-res-brief-recovery-link: SessionStart opens with a RESUME block a fresh agent can act on; DX-recover-brief-slice: a reserved recovery slice never cut by brief_max_tokens; AW-hook-delivery: status line at SessionStart; MTD-budget-test: lean 30,000 bytes / core 40,000 for tools/list while SE-mcp-budget and P-change-surface.context-budget still say 95,000-100,000 bytes and 'report only'; [session].context_budget_tokens default 40000 and doctor reports 28489 tokens now. Nothing says who wins when the sum exceeds the budget, and the 1K-char SessionStart cannot hold a charter, a RESUME block, a recovery slice and a status line. Question: one allocation table? RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: [session].context_budget_tokens is the only total; SessionStart <=1K chars carries the contract plus at most ONE dynamic line (resume, else pending approvals, else upgrade); everything else (requirements/policy charters, rules, recovery detail) is fetched via brief on request or at claim; GP-brief supersedes the separate requirements charter line once graded policies land; SE-mcp-budget and P-change-surface.context-budget are rewritten to the MTD per-profile numbers. Record as decision D-session-start-budget.
data.title: DECIDE (lead asks the operator): one budget for everything always loaded at session start

Two phases design the same capability: P-resume (2026-10-04, 9 B-res-* tasks, blocked behind the docs wave) and P-orphan-recovery (2026-10-18, D-orphan-recovery accepted, DX-recovery-* and DX-resume-command etc). The orphan-recovery research (docs/ddflow/research/orphan-recovery.md) never mentions P-resume. Concrete clashes: (a) two tasks build the CLI verb ddflow resume (B-res-resume, DX-resume-command); (b) B-res-resume: dead holder proved -> claim --force and adopt the worktree, [recover].auto = ask|safe(default)|always|off; D-orphan-recovery: ddflow applies only SAFE_AUTO actions, launcher resume off by default, kill switch [recover].enabled, recovery_attempts cap 2 — different knob names and a different takeover default; (c) brief/SessionStart recovery block twice (B-res-brief-recovery-link, DX-recover-brief-slice); (d) liveness evidence (B-res-heartbeat, DX-health-watch-liveness), in-flight gates (B-res-inflight-gates, DX-health-orphan-wait), merge landed/interrupted (B-res-merge-landed, B-res-merge-journal, DX-recovery-detectors). The pairs are linked related (not folded) until the operator chooses. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: D-orphan-recovery governs (later, operator-accepted, narrower takeover): fold B-res-resume into DX-resume-command, B-res-brief-recovery-link into DX-recover-brief-slice, B-res-heartbeat into DX-health-watch-liveness, B-res-inflight-gates into DX-health-orphan-wait; keep B-res-chaos-tests, B-res-driver, B-res-session-lifecycle, B-res-merge-journal; use the single knob family [recover] with enabled (kill switch) and auto = propose|safe; close P-resume when its remaining tasks are done. Record as decision D-recovery-one-design.
data.title: DECIDE (lead asks the operator): P-resume (B-res-*) versus P-orphan-recovery (DX-recovery-*), one recovery design

data.body: Contradiction found by the queue dedupe review 2026-10-23. D-mcp-tool-families (operator 2026-10-19/22) fixes 24 advertised tools: 9 hot + 15 noun families with an action enum; SE-mcp-budget says new commands join an existing action group and report their byte cost. About 17 open tasks still specify their own tool: B-goal-model (ddflow_goal), B-prop-model (ddflow_proposal), B-perf-bench (ddflow_perf), B-sched-author (ddflow_schedule), B-skills-events (ddflow_skill), B-sub-events (ddflow_agent), KB-config (kb_search, kb_get, kb_propose), LB-surfaces (one label tool), US-surfaces (one story tool), RQM-surfaces (ddflow_requirement), SPEC-surfaces, P-agent-caps.slots (ddflow_slot), P-context-sync.tell, P-safeguards.model, RM-run-tool-mcp (ddflow_run), PM-search-call (ddflow_search/ddflow_call); another ~80 say 'no new MCP tool (tools/list budget has ~45 bytes of headroom)', a premise voided by the diet. Question: may a new noun add a family (24 -> 24+n), or must it be an action of an existing family? RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: new record kinds are actions of ONE 'record' family (kind as argument), exceptions only for ddflow_run (the long-op poll) and the search/call facade; the ~45-byte boilerplate is deleted; each listed task is reworded to name its family action. Record as decision D-mcp-new-nouns.
data.title: DECIDE (lead asks the operator): do new record kinds add MCP tools or join families under the tool diet

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes, queue dedupe review). `ddflow dupes --open-only --limit 0` returns 5,298 pairs at the default floor; about 70% are the per-phase -docs/-surfaces/-eval/-e2e/-acceptance/-decide tasks, which share template wording by design (e.g. 40 'Document the X: README section, help topic, ...' tasks, 0.70-0.93), siblings inside one phase, or decisions against their own -r2/-r3 amendment (0.99 pairs that are superseded chains). The real overlaps found by hand (B-id-terms ~ ID-vocab-aliases, MTD-profiles ~ CP-mcp-profiles ~ P-agent-parity.tool-profile, PD-req-kind ~ RQM-model, P-resume ~ P-orphan-recovery) sit among them and the ledger of 'unsettled pairs' can never reach zero. Wanted: skip pairs whose ids share a family suffix (-docs, -surfaces, -eval, -e2e, -acceptance, -decide) across phases and same-phase siblings unless the score is >= 0.85; skip a decision pair when one supersedes or extends the other; report by cluster, not by pair; keep --distinct for the rest. Regression: a fixture with 5 template siblings and one true duplicate reports exactly one pair.
data.title: `ddflow dupes` cannot be settled: 5,298 pairs at floor 0.5, most template siblings and supersession chains

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). B-id-terms (2026-10-05) and ID-vocab-aliases (2026-10-22) both build ddflow/services/vocabulary.py and [vocabulary] with the same aliases; ID-vocab-aliases even says the service 'does not exist' and was created by moving a loose task (the --readd/move path), so the add-time check (D-no-duplicates) did not ask. RQM-model and PD-req-kind both define ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml. MTD-profiles said 'This IS P-agent-parity.tool-profile and CP-mcp-profiles' while needing them. Text similarity alone (Jaccard) scores these 0.3-0.5. Add structural signals to the dedupe score and to doctor's duplicate_work: the same declared glob or new-file path on two open tasks of different phases, the same MCP tool or CLI verb named in two bodies, an 'IS'/'subsumes' sentence naming an open task that is still in needs. Regression: two open tasks declaring the same new module path are offered as related/duplicate at add time, including through --readd and phase moves.
data.title: Duplicate score ignores shared globs, new-file targets and named modules: real duplicates filed unflagged

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). D-mcp-tool-families says it 'Amends D-mcp-surface-r2's no tool is renamed or merged' and D-DEP-Q1 says it 'adds a tier to D-compat-r2 (amended, not superseded)', but both targets stay accepted with their old clause, brief/decision applicable show the contradicting pair as equally binding, and the only machine relations are supersede (whole record) and link --extends (invisible in applicable). Wanted: `ddflow decision amend ID --clause TEXT --by NEW` (or `decision add --amends ID --clause`) that records the amended clause, shows it struck/annotated under the target in applicable/brief/show, and lists it in doctor; amending is not superseding so history and the unamended clauses stay binding. Regression: after D-DEP-Q1 amends D-compat-r2, `decision show D-compat-r2` and `decision applicable` for a surfaces file print the amendment beside the clause.
data.title: A decision that amends one clause of another leaves both accepted and contradicting; link --extends changes nothing a reader sees

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). `ddflow task fold ID-vocab-aliases B-id-terms` merged bodies and globs and re-pointed dependents, but the folded task's own needs (B-org-layers, ID-decide) were dropped; `fold P-agent-parity.tool-profile MTD-profiles` likewise dropped P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2, the real prerequisite of the cap-driven profile choice. Neither the dry run nor the result mentions it. Wanted: the dry run lists the needs the folded task had that the keeper lacks (and that are not already implied transitively) and `--carry-needs` (default on, with the cycle check the fold already has) adds them; the result prints what was carried. Regression: fold A (needs X) into B (needs Y) leaves B needing X and Y, and a cycle is refused as today.
data.title: task fold keeps the keeper's needs only: the folded task's prerequisites vanish silently

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). `ddflow abandon DX-suite-host-lock` (done in effect) printed 'warning: B-af-doctor, B-af-acceptance, B-par-process-isolation still need DX-suite-host-lock and can never start' and left them blocked until `ddflow update --needs` was run by hand for each; the same for DX-list-paging -> DX-record-verb-table. A needs edge to a task that ended abandoned is never satisfiable, so the queue silently grows dead items (doctor should count them, today only the abandon call prints it). Wanted: abandon takes `--drop-edges` (default prompt/refuse in non-interactive mode unless --repoint-to or --drop-edges is given), and `ddflow doctor` lists every open item that needs an abandoned item. Regression: abandoning a prerequisite with dependents and no flag exits 3 naming the two options; with --drop-edges the dependents' needs no longer name it.
data.title: abandon without --repoint-to leaves dependents that can never start; only a warning

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). Phase P1 (title 'P', test artefact, 0 of 1 tasks) cannot be closed (`phase close` is the phase pipeline: research, tasks, unit_tests, bug_hunt, dedupe, live_test, corrections, docs) and there is no `phase abandon`/`phase remove` verb. Tasks have `abandon` and `remove`; phases only add/list/close. Wanted: `ddflow phase abandon ID --reason` (refused while it has open tasks unless --repoint-to or --abandon-tasks), kept in history, hidden from status/list by default. Regression: an empty phase abandoned disappears from `list phase` and stays in `--state abandoned`.
data.title: No way to retire a throwaway phase: phase close demands the whole pipeline, there is no phase abandon

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). Open bugs B2ee8585e2d (stale pin), Ba502f5434a and B630ffef2d8 (test_remedy_texts after the approvals CLI landed) and Bff1731a132 (wait target) were already fixed on main and closed only by hand (`bug fixed --landed`), after their ready fix tasks had sat in the queue. DX-bug-repro-verify marks a bug unconfirmed until its repro fails at the recorded sha, but nothing re-runs the recorded repro/test against current main. Wanted: `ddflow bug recheck [ID|--all]` that runs each open bug's recorded repro command or named test on the base (bounded workers, detached via the run engine), reports 'no longer reproduces' with the first passing commit (git bisect over the test), and offers `bug fixed --landed SHA`; also a cadence job. Regression: a bug whose test passes on main is reported with the introducing commit and its fix task is listed for removal.
data.title: No sweep finds open bugs that are already fixed on main: four of 50 were stale

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). Closing DX-suite-host-lock, DX-list-paging, DX-verify-fix-already-landed and RV-split-cap as 'done in effect' required `ddflow abandon --reason "done in effect: <commit, test>"`, which counts them as abandoned in progress/metrics and phase completion, and puts the commit and test only in prose. Wanted: `ddflow task close ID --done-by SHA --evidence TEST[,TEST]` that verifies the commit is on the base and the named tests pass there (like bug fixed --landed), records state done with done_by, lets dependents proceed without a dead-edge warning, and shows in `ddflow show` and the phase tally as done. Regression: closing with a commit not on the base is refused; with a real one the dependents of the task become ready.
data.title: A task done in effect can only be 'abandoned': the record says dropped, not done, and the proof lives in free text

data.body: Seen 2026-10-23 (qa-dupes). M801fd9dc2b ('schedule.parallel = fixed, max_parallel_tasks = 6 ... return to auto when the lanes stop', 2026-10-07) still headed the brief's operational memory while .ddflow/local/config.toml says parallel = auto and status shows 'parallel: 13 (auto ...)'; Me5db019bea ('unit_tests uses pytest -n 24') is superseded by the computed '-n {workers}'; M1da6c78dd8 names a retired reviewer address. Wanted: `memory add --verify 'ddflow config get schedule.parallel' --expect fixed` and/or `--expires DATE`; the brief and doctor show 'memory M... contradicted by the machine' and offer `memory forget`. Regression: a memory whose verify command no longer matches is listed by doctor and dropped from the brief's operational memory.
data.title: Memories about machine state go stale silently: nothing expires or re-checks them

data.body:
Tasks and phases are caller-named (D-id-schemes-final covers imported ones only), so parallel agents pick different shapes (US-, RQM-, SPEC-, PI-, ACF-, LS-, SU- were each chosen by the researching agent; older phases use B-uni, P-agent..., fix-B...). Add an optional 'id_prefix' on a phase (set by phase add, a preset, or the org vocabulary) and have 'ddflow task add --phase P' with no id mint the next free <prefix>-<seq> through the id service (next_seq, taken-key check across worktrees), and with an explicit id warn or refuse a non-conforming prefix per [ids].enforce. Print the convention in the claim/brief charter so agents follow it, and in 'ddflow plan check' (warn on a plan whose task ids break the phase prefix). Org/company convention via the org layer (B-org-layers); presets via DX-id-vocabulary-aliases.

Moved from the loose task DX-id-phase-prefix-registry into phase P-id-consistency (a task cannot be re-parented); DX-id-phase-prefix-registry is abandoned with a pointer here.

NOTE 2026-10-23 (queue dedupe review, qa-dupes): the prefix ID- is already used by a DIFFERENT phase: ID-keep-busy, ID-retro and ID-triggers belong to P-continuous-improvement, while P-id-consistency's own tasks (ID-decide, ID-docs, ID-e2e, ID-templates-*, ID-conformance-lint, ID-alloc-test, ID-phase-prefix, ID-vocab-aliases folded) use ID- too. Two phases, one prefix - the exact collision this task exists to prevent. The prefix registry must refuse a second phase claiming a prefix, and one of the two families needs a new prefix (CI- is taken by CI-goals-loop; suggest IDC- for P-id-consistency or IMP- for continuous improvement). Ids already minted are not renamed here (P-reshape.rename).

data.body: Contradiction found by the queue dedupe review 2026-10-23. D-config-layer-order (operator 2026-10-18) is 'the single normative order for every layered thing (config knobs, workflow templates, rules, packs)': packaged < company defaults < user < project < machine-local < env < CLI < session < company enforced, later wins, a project may tighten an enforced floor and never loosen it. D-requirements-layers (operator 2026-10-21) defines requirement sources as org > team > project > local > task, tighten-only, with a 'team' layer that the single order does not have, written as a precedence of authority (org first) rather than as later-wins; RQM-layers builds it. D-CM-Q2 (commit policy) correctly follows D-config-layer-order. GP-org (graded policies) distributes policies in the org bundle with company floors, a third phrasing. Question: is the requirement layer chain a view of D-config-layer-order or a second order? RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: a view: org = layers 2 and 9 (defaults and enforced), team = a conf.d directory inside the project layer 4 (or the org bundle's team subset), project = 4, local = 5, task = the session overlay 8 scoped to one item; 'tighten-only' is the layer-9 floor rule applied to strength; no separate resolver. Record as decision D-requirements-layers-r2 (extends D-requirements-layers) and reword RQM-layers and GP-org to cite D-config-layer-order.
data.title: DECIDE (lead asks the operator): requirement layers org>team>project>local>task versus the one config layer order

data.body:
Wave tags are a derived graph attribute stored by hand: /tmp/claude-1001/restamp_api.py emits one ddflow update per task (886 then 779 updates in one restamp), and its pure-depth N disagrees with core.schedule.waves (glob-aware, used only by plancheck). Make depth (true dependency depth, counting only open prerequisites incl. inherited needs) and wave (glob-aware) first-class derived values from ItemGraph: ddflow list --wave N / --depth, a wave line in brief and status, JSON fields. Keep reading existing wave:N tags for compatibility, flag stale ones in doctor, and document that tags are no longer maintained by hand. Decide the one meaning of 'wave' with D-wave-semantics (accepted) and state it in the output. Retire the restamp scripts' role. Coordinate with DX-waves-status (open question).

Folded DX-wave-phase-prereq (Wave derivation counts a phase prerequisite as the wave of its last open task, and covers doc and research kinds): qa-graph finding is a correction to the very derivation GR-wave-derived builds (same core/schedule.py, it needed GR-wave-derived); one task, phase-prerequisite depth and doc/research kinds added to its scope.

Found by qa-graph 2026-10-23 (queue review). restamp_api.py (and so every wave:N tag stamped before 2026-10-23) counted a phase used as a prerequisite as 1 + the depth of the phase's OWN needs, ignoring its open tasks: a task behind a whole-phase hold such as P-docs-generic was stamped wave 1 when it cannot start until that phase's 9-deep chain is done (wave 10); 890 of 1581 tags were wrong, 6 to 28 waves too low, and doc and research kinds were not stamped at all. D-wave-semantics already says 'wave N = 1 + the highest wave among open prerequisites': make core.schedule depth (GR-wave-derived) implement that for phases: wave(phase) = max(wave of its open tasks, 1 + wave of its own needs); a task inherits its phase's needs; doc/research/job kinds count. Regression test: a task whose phase needs another phase with a 3-deep chain gets wave 4, not 1; a stale hand tag is reported by doctor. Reference implementation: docs/ddflow/research/scripts/wave_stamp_accurate.py (added by the queue review).
